header.title: The unit of trust is *the whole chain.*
header.lede: A finding or a green command alone is not proof. CodeVetter keeps task identity, execution, evidence, and uncertainty connected, so another engineer, or another agent, can re-check the result.

items.title: Task
items.body: Preserve the requested outcome and its acceptance boundary.

items.title: Change
items.body: Bind the exact agent revision, not “latest”.

items.title: Execute
items.body: Run the authoritative local checks the repository owns.

items.title: Evidence
items.body: Retain commands, bounded output, artifacts, and limits.

items.title: Verdict
items.body: Pass, fail, or unverified. Never a confidence score.

header.title: Proof that survives *the next question.*
header.lede: The public corpus measures a narrow recognition task. It is not evidence of production-wide accuracy or adoption, and the page says so.

items.title: Task identity first
items.body: The requested behavior and acceptance boundary stay attached to the run, so the verifier cannot quietly grade an easier task.

items.title: Exact change, not “latest”
items.body: Base and head identities, repository state, and the agent-produced patch travel with the evidence.

items.title: Executable checks decide
items.body: Repository-owned tests, builds, browser flows, API checks, and qualified workloads set the verdict boundary.

items.title: Evidence stays portable
items.body: Commands, bounded output, artifacts, status, and provenance live in machine-readable verification records.

items.title: Failures stay classified
items.body: Agent regressions stay separate from existing failures, environment problems, timeouts, and missing coverage.

items.title: Unknown is a real outcome
items.body: Missing or irrelevant evidence produces unverified, not a confidence score dressed up as success.

items.title: Point at the line *the verdict is about.*
items.body: A failing check is linked back to the exact change that caused it, with the command, the bounded output and the limitation, so a reviewer can confirm it in seconds instead of re-running everything.

items.title: Run the exact change from *your repository.*
items.body: The Apple-silicon release bundles the codevetter CLI and a local MCP sidecar inside the app. Provider-backed review needs a supported local agent CLI; repository-owned checks remain the verdict boundary.

code.label: zsh — ~/work/auth-service
code.code:
# bundled at /Applications/CodeVetter.app/Contents/MacOS/codevetter
$ codevetter check     --range main...HEAD     --task "Reject expired sessions"     --json

✗ fail        pnpm test auth/session.test.ts
✓ pass        pnpm typecheck
? unverified  browser refresh journey

blocks.title: Understand *the boundary.*
blocks.lede: Scope, evidence, and availability, answered plainly.

items.a: An execution-backed verification and evaluation system for coding agents. It connects a requested task and exact agent change to executable checks, retained evidence, explicit limitations, and a pass, fail, or unverified verdict.

items.q: Is it another AI code reviewer?
items.a: Review is one input, not the authority. A model can identify suspicious code and suggest what to test, but CodeVetter treats task-relevant execution evidence as the verdict boundary.

items.q: Does my repository go to a CodeVetter server?
items.a: No hosted verification backend is required. Product state and execution evidence stay local. If you start an optional provider-backed review, selected prompt and code context go directly to the provider you configured.
Local checks, stored evidence, and the desktop viewer work without a CodeVetter service. Reviews that call Anthropic, OpenAI, or OpenRouter still need network access to that provider.
Only the declared task and evidence boundary. A pass does not prove behavior that was never checked, and missing or irrelevant evidence stays unverified instead of becoming confidence.
The current GitHub release has an Apple-silicon macOS DMG and updater archive. Source is ISC-licensed. Other platform installers and a Homebrew cask are not published yet.
